title: The Wow! signal
description: A radio telescope catches something remarkable, and a handwritten Wow! gives it a name. SciShow Space introduces the 1977 detection and the search for a repeat. This 2015 explainer is a starting point, not a current verdict or proof of extraterrestrial contact.

connections.reason: One detection raises a bigger question: why does the rest of the universe seem so quiet?
What if a signal is a message, but you are not its intended listener?

title: Numbers stations: messages hiding in plain hearing
description: Voices read strings of numbers into the shortwave ether. Ringway Manchester explores spy communications and the listeners who document them. The broadcasts are real; an ordinary listener usually cannot identify the recipient or decode the message.

connections.reason: From secret recipients to a public challenge: who was Cicada recruiting?
Follow shortwave listening into the voices behind the Buzzer.
Can a message hide in full view, even outside CIA headquarters?

title: UVB-76: voices behind the buzz
description: Ringway Manchester examines voices and sounds associated with the shortwave station nicknamed the Buzzer. Listen for the human activity behind the eerie reputation. Claims that it is a doomsday switch remain speculation, not an established explanation.

connections.reason: A voice does not tell you who controls the signal. What happens when someone takes over a broadcast?
Compare the Buzzer with transmissions built around spoken codes.

title: The Max Headroom broadcast hijacking
description: Two Chicago television broadcasts were interrupted in 1987 by a masked intruder. The Reyna Bros. documentary examines the footage and the mystery behind it. The intrusion is documented; proposed identities should be treated as theories. Contains crude language and disturbing broadcast footage.

connections.reason: Compare this unidentified intruder with a solved TV hijacking and a supposed alien message.
An anonymous message can interrupt a street as well as a screen. Who wanted these words to be seen?
Here a sender was deliberate. With the Wow! signal, was there a sender at all?

title: The Great Silence
description: If the universe is so vast, why has contact proved so elusive? LEMMiNO explores the search for extraterrestrial intelligence in this 2018 documentary. Its scenarios are possibilities to consider, not evidence that anyone has contacted us.

connections.reason: If distant searches are quiet, what should we make of reported encounters closer to home?
Return to a specific detection that made the larger question feel urgent.

title: Extraordinary Until Proven Otherwise
description: LEMMiNO examines three widely circulated Navy UFO videos alongside witness accounts. This 2020 documentary captures the debate at that time; unidentified does not establish an extraterrestrial origin. Follow the footage, the testimony, and the gaps between them.

connections.reason: Step back from individual sightings to the larger question of extraterrestrial intelligence.
An unusual observation and an explicit claim of alien contact are different kinds of evidence. Compare them.
Disputed footage is not limited to the sky. What happens when the unidentified subject looks like an animal?
Follow unusual aerial sightings into the folklore surrounding Mothman.

title: Cicada 3301: An Internet Mystery
description: Anonymous puzzles draw strangers into cryptography, hidden messages, and a search for whoever is behind them. LEMMiNO reconstructs the trail in this 2018 documentary. Proposed identities and motives remain theories within this account.

connections.reason: Another deliberately constructed cipher: what changes when the author is known?
Compare public puzzles with codes intended for a select audience.
Leave the screen and follow cryptic messages into city streets.

title: Kryptos: the code outside CIA headquarters
description: LEMMiNO traces the sculpture and the decades spent trying to read its hidden messages. This 2024 documentary predates the discovery of K4 plaintext in archival papers in 2025. Finding the text and reconstructing the cipher method are different achievements.

connections.reason: Kryptos has a named creator. How does a puzzle change when its organizers stay anonymous?
Another public object carrying an obscure message, but is it meant to be decoded?

title: The Toynbee tiles: messages underfoot
description: Cryptic tiles embedded in city streets turn a walk into an investigation. Spektator follows the messages and the efforts to explain them. This account presents an investigation and proposed attribution, not permission to treat every theory as established fact.

connections.reason: Compare scattered physical clues with a puzzle that spread from the internet into the world.
Both force an unexpected message into everyday life. What can the delivery method tell us?

title: Captain Midnight and the alien broadcast
description: Oddity Archive compares the 1986 HBO intrusion with the 1977 Southern Television interruption. One was a pricing protest by an identified operator; the other carried a voice claiming extraterrestrial authority. That claim is part of the broadcast, not evidence of alien contact.

connections.reason: Return to the broadcast intrusion whose masked performer remains the central mystery.
Compare someone claiming alien authority with witnesses trying to describe something unidentified.
Not every strange transmission is an intrusion. Some have an intended audience all along.

title: Sasquatch: unraveling the sightings
description: Monstrum explores how Sasquatch stories, reported encounters, and disputed footage shaped the modern Bigfoot legend. Follow the history of the claims without mistaking their popularity for proof of an undiscovered animal.

connections.reason: From a figure in the forest to a shape on the water: compare two legends shaped by disputed images.
What can a short recording establish? Compare Bigfoot footage with the debate around Navy UFO videos.

title: Loch Ness: beneath the surface
description: Monstrum follows the history of Nessie and the photographs, theories, and searches surrounding the lake. A tour through a persistent mystery and its explanations, rather than a claim that a monster has been found.

connections.reason: How much of a creature can we infer from an ambiguous image? Compare Nessie with Sasquatch.
Leave the lake for a town where reported sightings became a very different kind of local legend.

title: Mothman: the winged legend of Point Pleasant
description: Monstrum examines the reported winged figure and the folklore that grew around Point Pleasant. Separate witness stories and later interpretations from established events; associations with disasters do not establish prediction or causation.

connections.reason: Compare two American creature legends and the ways communities retell encounters.
A strange figure in the sky opens another path: how do witnesses describe something they cannot identify?
